bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 248` in `ot::Message::Write`. The staged 297-byte `ip6-send-fuzzer` witness contains CoAP URI path `a/sd`; after the CoAP payload marker `ff`, the request body begins `0a ad`, i.e. `ThreadTlv::kThreadNetworkData` with advertised length 173, so IPv6/UDP/CoAP parsing reaches `ot::NetworkData::Leader::HandleServerData()`, which extracts a `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` from the request payload and forwards its raw bytes plus length into `RegisterNetworkData()`. By the time `RegisterNetworkData()` signals `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`, the leader network-data buffer `mTlvs` must occupy the full `NetworkData::kMaxSize == 255`; the staged static artifacts do not isolate which final `AddNetworkData()` / `Insert()` call reaches byte 255 or which persisted bytes later occupy `mTlvs[0:2]`, but that exact 255-byte state is forced by the one-line fix and the later serialization edge case. The queued notifier callback drives `Mle::HandleStateChanged()` into `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()`, which builds a multicast Data Response for `ff02::1` and selects `Tlv::kNetworkData`, so `AppendNetworkData()` serializes full leader network data. `FillNetworkDataTlv()` initializes `length` to 255, `GetNetworkData(false, aTlv.GetNetworkData(), length)` copies all 255 bytes from persisted `mTlvs` into stack `NetworkDataTlv tlv`, and `aTlv.SetLength(255)` writes the generic TLV extended-length marker into a base MLE TLV header. When `Message::AppendTlv(tlv)` asks `ot::Tlv::GetSize()` for the serialized size, generic TLV logic treats `tlv` as an `ExtendedTlv` and reinterprets the first two bytes already present in `mNetworkData` as a 16-bit length field, so the append size exceeds the real 257-byte stack object. `Message::Write()` then executes `memcpy(..., aBuf, bytesToCopy)` while `aBuf` still points into stack `tlv`, producing the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow READ at `src/core/common/message.cpp:601`. The patch fixes this by lowering `NetworkData::kMaxSize` from 255 to 254 so base MLE Network Data TLVs never carry the reserved length byte 255.

source.description: First project-side parse on the crashing path that materializes attacker-controlled Thread Network Data bytes into stack object `networkData`.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `gt_results/arvo_17147/poc` is 297 bytes long. Its bytes include ASCII `a/sd`; after the CoAP payload marker `ff`, the request body begins `0a ad`, which matches `ThreadTlv::kThreadNetworkData` (type 10) with advertised length `0xad` (173). Once CoAP dispatches to the Server Data resource, this statement materializes that TLV into `networkData`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `Write()` copies from stack `NetworkDataTlv tlv` using an append size that generic TLV logic inflated beyond the object's real extent.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report identifies `tlv` in `ot::Mle::Mle::AppendNetworkData` as the overrun stack object and reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 248` at `message.cpp:601` through `__asan_memcpy`.

root_cause.code: kMaxSize = 255, ///< Maximum size of Thread Network Data in bytes.
root_cause.description: The maximum leader network-data size is defined as 255 even though generic base TLVs only allow lengths up to 254 and reserve 255 as the extended-length marker. Allowing leader network data to reach 255 makes later MLE Network Data serialization encode a base TLV with the reserved length byte, which generic `ot::Tlv::GetSize()` then misinterprets as an `ExtendedTlv`.
root_cause.note: The fixing diff changes this exact constant from 255 to 254.

tainted_value_origin.description: The current Server Data request's Thread Network Data TLV bytes and advertised length are forwarded into leader registration here. On the crashing run this untrusted state participates in leaving persistent leader network data at the exact edge case `mLength == 255`, which is the required precursor to the later reserved-length serialization bug.

parser_admitted.description: The CoAP option parser has already reconstructed URI path `a/sd` from the staged request and matched the Server Data resource, so execution dispatches into `Leader::HandleServerData()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The received IPv6/UDP payload is admitted as a CoAP request on URI `a/sd` and dispatched to the Server Data resource.
Leader-side Server Data handling extracts the request's `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` into stack `networkData` and forwards its raw TLVs plus a sender-derived RLOC16 into `RegisterNetworkData()`.

Registration merges the incoming network data into persistent leader state and raises `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`; on the crashing run the resulting leader buffer reaches the exact edge case `mLength == 255`.

The queued notifier callback processes `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA`, routes execution into `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()`, and builds a multicast Data Response that requests the full Network Data TLV.
AppendNetworkData copies the full 255-byte leader network data into stack `NetworkDataTlv tlv` and records base TLV length 255 in that temporary object.

Generic TLV size logic interprets that length byte 255 as an extended TLV marker, reuses the first two bytes of the copied leader-network-data buffer as a 16-bit length field, and `Message::Write()` overreads stack `tlv` while copying the oversized append length.

fine_trace.note: Source. After CoAP dispatch on URI `a/sd`, this parser copies the request's Thread Network Data TLV into stack `networkData`. In the staged witness, the bytes after the CoAP payload marker `ff` begin `0a ad`, so the current request advertises `ThreadTlv::kThreadNetworkData` (type 10) with body length 173.

The handler derives `aRloc16` from the sender address's low 16 bits and forwards the current 173-byte network-data span into leader registration. The immediately preceding `networkData.IsValid()` cannot reject malformed inner bytes because `ThreadNetworkDataTlv::IsValid()` always returns true.

By the time registration raises this flag, it has already merged the request's network-data entries into persistent leader buffer `mTlvs`. On the crashing run that persisted buffer must now occupy exactly 255 bytes: the patch only lowers `NetworkData::kMaxSize` from 255 to 254, and the later `aTlv.SetLength(length)` edge is only dangerous when `length == 255`. The staged static artifacts do not isolate which final `AddNetworkData()` / `Insert()` write reaches byte 255, whether registration used the `rlocIn` or `!rlocIn` arm, or which persisted bytes at `mTlvs[0:2]` came from this specific request.
When the queued notifier callback processes the network-data-change flag on this leader/full-thread-device instance, execution enters `HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter()`.
This state-change path prepares a one-element TLV selector `{Tlv::kNetworkData}` and the multicast destination `ff02::1`, then sends an unsolicited Data Response.

The single selector from step 5 takes the `kNetworkData` arm. For the multicast destination `ff02::1`, this path uses `stableOnly = false`, so the full leader network data is serialized instead of a reduced stable subset.

fine_trace.code: kMaxSize = 255, ///< Maximum size of Thread Network Data in bytes.
fine_trace.note: Root cause. Leader network data is allowed to grow to 255 bytes even though generic base TLVs only permit lengths up to `ot::Tlv::kBaseTlvMaxLength == 254`; the value 255 is reserved as `kExtendedLength`. The patch fixes the bug by lowering this constant to 254 so later MLE serialization never emits a base TLV length byte of 255.
AppendNetworkData builds a stack `NetworkDataTlv tlv` and initializes the output-length variable to 255, because MLE `NetworkDataTlv` reserves `mNetworkData[255]` bytes.

With `aStableOnly == false` from step 6 and the persisted leader state from step 3, this call copies all 255 bytes of `mTlvs` into stack `tlv.mNetworkData` and leaves `length == 255`. The saved artifacts prove the current request reached this 255-byte persisted state, but they do not isolate which bytes inside the copied buffer originated in the current request.
The temporary MLE Network Data TLV records a base TLV length byte of 255. That byte value is also the generic `ot::Tlv` extended-length marker.
Serialization now passes the stack `tlv` through generic TLV size logic. The append size is no longer bounded by `sizeof(tlv)`; it will trust the meaning of the stored length byte from step 10.

fine_trace.code:
return IsExtended() ? sizeof(ExtendedTlv) + static_cast<const ExtendedTlv *>(this)->GetLength()
                    : sizeof(Tlv) + GetLength();
fine_trace.note: Because step 10 stored length 255, `IsExtended()` is true here and `GetSize()` reinterprets the first two bytes of `tlv.mNetworkData` as an extended 16-bit length field. Those are whatever persisted leader-network-data bytes step 9 copied into the temporary object; the staged artifacts do not prove they originated in the current request. On the crashing run the derived append size is larger than the real 257-byte stack object.

Sink. `Message::Append` forwards the oversized length from step 12 into `Write` while `aBuf` still points into step 8's stack `tlv`. On the crashing copy iteration `bytesToCopy` exceeds the remaining bytes in that 257-byte object, so this `memcpy()` reads past `tlv`; ASan reports `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 248` here and identifies `tlv` in `AppendNetworkData()` as the overrun stack object.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved ASan stack directly covers fine-trace steps 4-13 (`HandleStateChanged -> HandleNetworkDataUpdateRouter -> SendDataResponse -> AppendNetworkData -> FillNetworkDataTlv -> AppendTlv -> GetSize -> Write`). Earlier source/materialization steps 1-3 are reconstructed from the only `a/sd` Server Data handler that forwards `ThreadNetworkDataTlv` into `RegisterNetworkData()`. The staged artifacts do not isolate which final `AddNetworkData()` / `Insert()` call makes `mLength` reach 255 or which persisted bytes later occupy `mTlvs[0:2]`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes, at the state level. The `a/sd` request's Thread Network Data TLV is parsed in step 1 and forwarded to `RegisterNetworkData()` in step 2; on the crashing run that registration path leaves persisted leader network data at `mLength == 255` in step 3. Steps 9-12 then copy that 255-byte persisted buffer into stack `tlv`, write the reserved length marker 255, and reinterpret the first two copied bytes as an extended length. The saved artifacts do not isolate whether those two bytes originated in this specific request.

format.name: OpenThread ip6-send CoAP Server Data request
format.contract: A single `ip6-send-fuzzer` input whose bytes after the harness link-security flag decode to an IPv6/UDP CoAP POST on URI `a/sd` carrying a `ThreadTlv::kThreadNetworkData` TLV; in the saved witness, the CoAP payload marker `ff` is followed by `0a ad`, i.e. type 10 with length 173. The required trigger condition is that `RegisterNetworkData()` leaves leader network data length exactly 255 before `OT_CHANGED_THREAD_NETDATA` is processed. That singular 255-byte state is required so `AppendNetworkData()` emits a base MLE Network Data TLV with length byte 255 and generic `Tlv::GetSize()` treats it as an extended TLV.
